subject: Mathematics
title: Algebra Foundations
source_note: Bounded set covering the NAMED distinctions a first algebra course rests on: the two averages, the parts of an expression, the two intercepts, factors against multiples, perimeter against area, and an equation against an expression. Deliberately not arithmetic. The grader attributes a spoken answer to the nearest candidate in a closed set of named answers, so a card whose answer is a number has nothing to be confused WITH and no misconception to name. What this set can diagnose is a student reaching for the wrong CONCEPT; what it cannot diagnose is a slip in the working.

cards.question: What do you call the middle value of a data set once the values are put in order?
cards.hint: You line the numbers up and walk to the middle one.
cards.explanation: The median is the middle value once the data is ordered, so an extreme value barely moves it.
cards.misconception: The median is the middle of the ordered list; the mean is the total shared out evenly.

cards.question: What do you call the total of all the values divided by how many there are?
cards.hint: You add everything up, then share it out.
cards.explanation: The mean adds every value and divides by the count, so one extreme value drags it.
cards.misconception: The mean is the total shared out evenly; the median is the middle of the ordered list.

cards.question: In the expression 7x, what do you call the number 7 multiplying the variable?
cards.hint: It is attached to the letter and multiplies it.
cards.explanation: A coefficient is the number multiplying a variable, so in 7x the coefficient is 7.
cards.misconception: A coefficient multiplies a variable; a constant stands alone with no variable attached.

cards.question: In the expression 7x plus 4, what do you call the number 4 standing on its own?
cards.hint: It never changes, whatever the letter turns out to be.
cards.explanation: A constant term has no variable attached, so its value does not change with x.
cards.misconception: A constant stands alone; a coefficient is the number multiplying a variable.

cards.question: What do you call the point where a graph crosses the horizontal axis?
cards.hint: It is where the height is zero.
cards.explanation: At the x-intercept the graph meets the horizontal axis, so y is zero there.
cards.misconception: The x-intercept is where y is zero; the y-intercept is where x is zero.

cards.question: What do you call the point where a graph crosses the vertical axis?
cards.hint: It is where you have gone nowhere sideways yet.
cards.explanation: At the y-intercept the graph meets the vertical axis, so x is zero there.
cards.misconception: The y-intercept is where x is zero; the x-intercept is where y is zero.

cards.question: What do you call a whole number that divides exactly into a given number?
cards.hint: It fits into the number without a remainder.
cards.explanation: A factor divides a number exactly, so the factors of 12 include 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
cards.misconception: A factor divides into the number; a multiple is what you get by multiplying it up.

cards.question: What do you call a number you reach by multiplying a given number by a whole number?
cards.hint: You count up in that number to reach it.
cards.explanation: A multiple comes from multiplying, so the multiples of 3 are 3, 6, 9, 12 and onwards.
cards.misconception: A multiple is reached by multiplying up; a factor divides into the number.

cards.question: What do you call the total distance all the way around the outside of a shape?
cards.hint: You walk right around the edge and add as you go.
cards.explanation: The perimeter is the total length of the boundary, so it is measured in ordinary length units.
cards.misconception: The perimeter is the distance around the edge; the area is the surface the shape covers.

cards.question: What do you call the amount of surface a flat shape covers?
cards.hint: It is how much floor the shape would cover.
cards.explanation: The area measures the surface covered, so it is given in square units.
cards.misconception: The area is the surface covered; the perimeter is the distance around the edge.

cards.question: What do you call two expressions joined by an equals sign?
cards.hint: It makes a claim that two things are the same.
cards.explanation: An equation states that two expressions are equal, which is what lets you solve for the unknown.
cards.misconception: An equation has an equals sign and can be solved; an expression has none and can only be simplified.

cards.question: What do you call a group of terms with no equals sign, which you can only simplify?
cards.hint: Nothing is being claimed equal to anything.
cards.explanation: An expression is a combination of terms with no equals sign, so it can be simplified but not solved.
cards.misconception: An expression has no equals sign and cannot be solved; an equation does and can.
